Aggressive therapy to lower low-density lipoprotein

Intermediate-density lipoprotein is the remnant of very-low-density lipoprotein and is not the particle behind eruptive xanthomas.
Chylomicrons or very-low-density lipoprotein

Low-density lipoprotein or lipoprotein(a)
High low-density lipoprotein goes with tendinous xanthomas on the Achilles, patella and back of the hand, not eruptive papules.
High-density lipoprotein or apolipoprotein A-I
High-density lipoprotein and its structural apolipoprotein A-I are protective and produce no xanthomas; the eruptive form reflects the triglyceride-rich particles.

opts: Low-density lipoprotein
Correct. Low-density lipoprotein, high in cholesterol, has the highest risk; very-low-density lipoprotein (high in triglyceride) has an increased risk, and high-density lipoprotein a decreased risk.

Very-low-density lipoprotein is high in triglyceride and carries an increased risk, but it ranks below the cholesterol-rich low-density class.
High-density lipoprotein
High-density lipoprotein carries a decreased risk because it transports cholesterol back to the liver, clearing away plaque.

Chylomicrons carry dietary triglyceride after a meal; the class singled out as highest risk is the cholesterol-rich low-density one.

They make statins unnecessary
Primary causes such as familial hypercholesterolemia usually need high-intensity statins, so finding one does not remove the need.

opts: When clinical atherosclerotic disease is already present
Established disease is secondary prevention with a high-intensity statin; calcium scoring is a primary-prevention tie-breaker.
When diabetes is present at age 40 to 75 years
Diabetes at 40 to 75 with low-density lipoprotein 70 or more already calls for a statin without calculating risk.
When an intermediate-risk statin decision is uncertain
Correct. In adults 40 to 75 without diabetes, low-density lipoprotein 70 to 189 and 10-year risk 7.5% to 19.9%, calcium scoring is considered if the statin decision is uncertain.
When low-density lipoprotein is 190 mg/dL or more

set1.q: Which apolipoprotein is made by the intestines and found in chylomicrons?
opts: Apolipoprotein E
Apolipoprotein E is important in triglyceride metabolism and critical in triglyceride clearance; its mutation causes familial dysbetalipoproteinemia.
Apolipoprotein B-48

Correct. Apolipoprotein B-48 is synthesized by the intestines and found in chylomicrons, while B-100 is made by the liver and found in very-low-density, intermediate-density and low-density lipoprotein and lipoprotein(a).
Apolipoprotein B-100
Apolipoprotein B-100 is made by the liver and found in very-low-density, intermediate-density and low-density lipoprotein and in lipoprotein(a), not in chylomicrons.
Apolipoprotein A-I
Apolipoprotein A-I is the major structural protein of high-density lipoprotein and is found on all of its particles, not on chylomicrons.

opts: High-density lipoprotein of 60 or more
High-density lipoprotein of 60 or more is protective and is a negative risk factor rather than an enhancer.
A coronary calcium score of zero
A zero calcium score lowers the estimated risk and may justify withholding a statin; it is not an enhancer.
Low-density lipoprotein under 100
An optimal low-density lipoprotein under 100 does not enhance risk; persistent elevation of 160 or more does.
Persistent triglyceride of 175 or more

Rise in high-density lipoprotein

Screening is meant to find the abnormality in the first place, so it is driven by overall cardiovascular risk rather than a prior result.
Visible skin xanthomas
Most patients have no signs, so waiting for xanthomas would miss them; overall cardiovascular risk drives screening.
Body weight alone

The score is uninterpretable

High low-density, normal triglyceride, high total

Yellow plaques on the eyelids near the inner canthus are xanthelasmas, which usually indicate an underlying genetic condition.
Back, buttocks and extensor limbs
Correct. They are clusters of small yellowish-white papules on the back, buttocks and extensor surfaces of the arms and legs, alongside lipemia retinalis and pancreatitis.
